items.definition: Wheat grain ground into a fine powder. It is the main part of the bread.
items.example: Flour is made from wheat at the mill.

items.definition: A tiny living fungus that eats sugar in the flour and makes gas.
items.example: We woke up the yeast in warm water for ten minutes.

items.definition: The soft, sticky mix of flour and water before it is baked.
items.example: I put the dough in a bowl and covered it.

items.definition: Pushing and folding the dough so it becomes smooth and strong.
items.example: Kneading the dough for five minutes feels strange at first.

items.definition: The resting time when the dough grows bigger because of the yeast.
items.example: The dough is proving now, so it will be ready in an hour.

items.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten after you wake up.
items.example: Breakfast is ready, so please sit down.

items.definition: The feeling you get when your body wants food and needs energy.
items.example: I am hungry, so I will have some bread.

items.definition: Grain that you pour into milk and eat with a spoon.
items.example: I ate cereal with cold milk.

items.definition: Bread that is warmed until it is brown and crisp.
items.example: I put jam on my toast.

items.definition: The capacity to do work or cause change.
The one you like most of all, the one you hope to see on the table.
items.example: My favourite food is spring rolls.

items.definition: To not like something. Nobody is wrong for disliking a food.
items.example: I dislike the smell of fish.

items.definition: What your tongue tells you when you eat. Sweet, sour, salty and bitter are the four main tastes.
items.example: The taste of this mango is very sweet.

items.definition: A part of a plant that holds seeds and is good to eat, like a mango or a pear.
items.example: A mango and a pear are both fruit.

items.definition: Ready to eat, sweet and soft. A green mango is not ripe yet.
items.example: This banana is yellow and ripe.

items.definition: The outside skin of a fruit. You usually peel it before eating.
items.example: I peel the orange before I eat it.

items.definition: A tiny helper in food that keeps your body working well. Fruit has plenty of vitamins.
items.example: One orange gives me lots of vitamin C.

items.definition: A place where milk is cleaned, heated and packed into bottles and cartons.
items.example: Our milk comes from the dairy near the town.

items.definition: The bag under a cow's body where the milk is made.
items.example: The farmer washes the cow's udder before milking.

items.definition: Heated quickly to kill tiny germs, so the milk stays safe to drink.
items.example: This milk is pasteurised, so it is safe to drink.

items.definition: A mineral from food that makes your bones and teeth strong.
items.example: Milk is full of calcium, and calcium keeps my bones strong.

items.definition: A measure of liquid. There are 1000 millilitres in one litre.
items.example: I drink one litre of milk every week.

items.definition: To cut something into thin, flat pieces.
items.example: I slice the banana and put it on top.

items.definition: To cut something into small cubes.
items.example: Please dice the mango for the salad.

items.definition: The liquid water inside a fruit.
items.example: I squeeze some lime juice over the fruit.

items.definition: To make something cold so it tastes fresh.
items.example: We chill the salad in the fridge for one hour.

items.definition: A small amount of food that you eat between two meals.
items.example: I brought a snack to school for break time.

items.definition: To deal with something in a particular way.
The part of food your body cannot digest. It helps your tummy work and keeps you full.
items.example: Wholemeal bread has more fibre than white bread.

items.definition: The building material of your body. It helps you grow and keeps you full for longer.
items.example: Eggs are full of protein, so they are a good snack.

items.definition: The same operation has been applied to both sides.
items.example: The equation stays balanced if you add the same number to both sides.

items.definition: A plant we eat for the part that is not the seed, like a carrot or a cabbage.
items.example: Broccoli and carrot are both vegetables.

items.definition: The part of a plant that grows down into the soil, to hold it up and drink water.
items.example: The root drank the rain deep in the ground.

items.definition: The flat green part of a vegetable that we eat, like cabbage or spinach.
items.example: She washed the leaves in the sink.

items.definition: The firm stem that holds leaves up. Broccoli and bok choy grow on one.
items.example: I eat the stalk of the broccoli too.

items.definition: To cook small pieces of food quickly in a little oil over a hot fire.
items.example: We stir-fry the morning glory for five minutes.
